title: Tyre Don Burst!

lines.text: Oshodi, no go-slow today?! Ah, God don butter my bread!
Sixty kilometre, AC cold, music sweet... today na my day o!
Jesus! Wetin be that?! Na my village people?!
Oga, calm down! Na your tyre burst. Na that panic dey cause accident.
Ah! FRSC?! Where you come from?!
Leave that one. Oga, hold your steering with two hands. Keep am straight. No slam brake o!
Two: comot leg for accelerator small-small. Make the motor slow down by itself.
Three: on your hazard light, make everybody know say wahala dey.
Four: when you don slow, enter side gently. Park far from the road.
Na me go change the tyre?
If you sabi and the place safe, use your spare. If not, call vulcanizer. And no stand near the road!
For night, some boys dey throw nail and stone for road. Use your full light when road empty, but dim am when motor dey come.
If tyre burst for dark place, no stop there. Drive slowly reach filling station or bright place. Rim cheap pass your life!
Officer, wetin I suppose carry for my boot?
Spare tyre, jack, C-caution, fire extinguisher. And check your tyre pressure every week.
Officer, thank you! Abeg, you no go collect anything?

end_card: Tyre wey burst no be the real problem. Na when your panic make you do wrong thing.
facts_note: Tyre blowout: grip the wheel with both hands and keep straight; don't brake hard; ease off the accelerator and let the car slow; hazard lights on; steer gently to a safe spot off the road; stand away from traffic; place the warning triangle (C-caution). At night use high beam only when no oncoming traffic; if a blowout happens in a dark/isolated spot, drive slowly on the flat to a lit, busy place. FRSC-listed items include spare tyre, jack, wheel spanner, C-caution, fire extinguisher, first aid kit. Cartoon character; not an official FRSC message.
